record.context_brief: injectivity of completed principal symbol map
record.original_question: For the continuous principal symbol map sigma-bar: Psi-bar^{0,-infinity}(M, F, E) -> S-bar^0(G_FN, L(pi^*E) tensor |T G_N|^{1/2}) arising in transverse pseudodifferential calculus on a compact foliated manifold, which geometric or analytic hypotheses guarantee that sigma-bar is injective?

evidence.quote: We have much less information on the principal symbol map in transverse pseudodifferential calculus. For instance, answers to the following questions are unknown. Question 3.10. Under which conditions is the principal symbol map sigma-bar injective?

By [24], this homomorphism is surjective, but, in general, is not injective. It is injective for any E if the groupoid G is amenable... Therefore, if G is not amenable, we cannot expect that sigma-bar is injective.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,F)$ be a compact foliated manifold with holonomy groupoid $G$, and let $G_F^N$ denote the associated transverse groupoid (the holonomy groupoid restricted to a complete transversal, or equivalently the normal/transverse groupoid). Let $E\to M$ be a smooth Hermitian vector bundle, and let $\pi:T^*G_F^N\to G_F^N$ (or the appropriate projection to the transverse cotangent bundle) be the canonical projection. Consider the algebra $\overline{\Psi}^{0,-\infty}(M,F,E)$ obtained as the closure of the algebra of order-zero transverse pseudodifferential operators with smoothing tangential part acting on sections of $E$, in the operator norm. Let
$$\overline{\sigma}:\overline{\Psi}^{0,-\infty}(M,F,E)\;\longrightarrow\;\overline{S}^{\,0}\!\left(G_F^N,\;\mathcal{L}(\pi^*E)\otimes |TG_N|^{1/2}\right)$$
be the continuous extension of the transverse principal symbol map to these completions, where $\overline{S}^{\,0}$ denotes the corresponding closure of the symbol algebra and $|TG_N|^{1/2}$ is the half-density bundle along the units of the transverse groupoid. It is known that $\overline{\sigma}$ is always surjective, and that it is injective whenever the groupoid $G$ is amenable (so in particular non-amenability of $G$ is an obstruction to injectivity).

Determine geometric or analytic conditions on $(M,F)$, on the groupoid $G$, and/or on the bundle $E$, that are sufficient (and ideally also necessary) to guarantee that the completed transverse principal symbol map $\overline{\sigma}$ is injective.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for subsequent work on the transverse pseudodifferential calculus on foliated manifolds (Kordyukov and others, including later work on Egorov's theorem and on principal symbol calculus on contact manifolds) does not turn up a general characterization of when the completed transverse principal symbol map is injective beyond the previously known sufficient condition that the holonomy groupoid be amenable. No paper appears to resolve the question in general, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Egorov theorem for transverse Dirac-type operators on foliated manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Egorov-type theorem for transverse pseudodifferential operators on foliations; works at the level of principal symbols but does not address injectivity of the completed symbol map.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops the calculus but does not characterize injectivity of the completed principal symbol map.

status_evidence.title: Functional calculus for tangentially elliptic operators on foliated manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Foliated pseudodifferential calculus relating principal symbols to groupoid C*-algebras; injectivity is known under amenability.
status_evidence.claim: Known sufficient condition is amenability of the holonomy groupoid; the general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Principal Symbol Calculus on Contact Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Recent monograph on principal symbol calculus in a related noncommutative setting; does not resolve the foliated transverse case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work does not provide a complete answer for transverse foliated case.
